title: Right-sized retry profiles and idempotency key guidance for streaming and unary SDK calls
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Background:
Redwood SDK users in Python/TypeScript/Go keep running into two related pain points: too-aggressive client retries that cause duplicate effects for non-idempotent server operations, and awkward streaming resume semantics that make ergonomic client code difficult. Existing artifacts in the repo define retry taxonomies and idempotency patterns, but we need a compact, cross-language set of defaults and migration guidance that: (1) minimizes accidental duplicated side-effects, (2) surfaces clear patterns for when to require user-provided idempotency keys, and (3) provides practical defaults for streaming resume tokens and per-language ergonomics.

Goal:
- Define a small set of retry profiles (none, conservative, throughput-friendly) with explicit backoff/timeouts for each SDK (Python/TS/Go).
- Specify canonical idempotency key behavior, header/param names, when SDK should auto-generate keys, and how to surface key usage to callers.
- Provide a retryable error taxonomy mapping HTTP/gRPC/net errors -> safe/unsafe/conditional retry buckets.
- Provide streaming resume recommendations (resume token shape, placement, and SDK helpers) and samples.
- Create migration path + opt-in feature flags to flip aggressive defaults for high-throughput customers.

Acceptance criteria:
- PR implementing default retry profiles and config surface in Python, TS, Go SDKs merged (or stubs merged with tests).
- Documentation page in SDK docs with examples for unary and streaming calls (including resume snippet).
- Benchmarks showing latency tail increase <10% for default conservative profile under contention.
- Playbook notes for platform team on when to enforce server-side idempotency checks.

Proposed retry profiles (cross-SDK):
1) none
   - Description: no automatic retries beyond a single attempt.
   - Use-cases: webhook-style fire-and-forget, callers that implement their own idempotency or want strict exactly-once.
   - Backoff/timeout: no retry; per-call timeout is SDK-level default (see below).
2) conservative (default)
   - Description: safe defaults for most customers prioritizing correctness over throughput.
   - Retryable errors: network disconnects, DNS failures, connection resets, 5xx (excluding 501/505), 429 (rate-limit, but with small cap), gRPC Unavailable/DeadlineExceeded.
   - Backoff: initial 100ms, multiplier 2.0, jitter (full jitter), max backoff 2s, max attempts 3.
   - Per-call timeout: 30s (unary); streaming: keep-alive heartbeats + idle timeout 60s.
3) throughput-friendly
   - Description: for high-throughput endpoints where retries increase qps and are cost-effective.
   - Backoff: initial 20ms, multiplier 1.7, jitter (none/less), max backoff 500ms, max attempts 5.
   - Per-call timeout: 60s (unary); streaming: aggressive reconnect with short resume window.

Idempotency key conventions:
- Canonical header name: Idempotency-Key (HTTP) / metadata "idempotency-key" (gRPC).
- For operations that are naturally non-idempotent (create with server-side side-effects): SDK SHOULD NOT retry automatically under the conservative profile unless an idempotency key is supplied by caller.
- Auto-generation rules: SDK may auto-generate a client idempotency key when the caller uses a high-level convenience method explicitly documented as idempotent-safe (e.g., upload-with-retry), otherwise the SDK MUST surface an explicit parameter to pass an idempotency key.
- Key format: v1 prefix + base64url(random-128bit) + timestamp (ISO date) -> e.g., "v1-3f1b2c...-2026-03-14T12:02:00Z". This makes keys debuggable but opaque enough to avoid collision concerns.
- TTL: servers should keep idempotency ledgers for 24 hours by default; document expectations if customer needs longer.

Retryable error taxonomy (mapping & guidance):
- Safe-auto-retry (SDK may retry under conservative profile):
  - Network-level errors: connection reset, connection refused (transient), DNS lookup failed, TLS handshake timed out.
  - Transport-level transient: HTTP 502/503/504, gRPC Unavailable, gRPC ResourceExhausted (with backoff), HTTP 429 (rate-limit) MAY be retried but with conservative caps.
- Conditional-retry (require idempotency key or explicit caller opt-in):
  - HTTP 500 on a request that may have been accepted by server (ambiguous success): require idempotency key.
  - gRPC Aborted/Unknown depending on server semantics: require idempotency key or server-side dedupe.
- Unsafe to retry automatically:
  - Client errors (400, 401, 403) except signature/time drift cases that can be transparently refreshed.
  - 501 Not Implemented, 505 HTTP Version Not Supported.
  - Application-level partial success responses (e.g., partial file commit) – SDK should surface to caller and not retry.

Streaming resume semantics and ergonomics:
- Resume token shape: base64url(JSON) containing {stream_id, last_sequence, last_ack_ts, optional_server_nonce}; SDKs should treat token as opaque but validate base64 decode.
- Placement: server includes resume token in wrapper message or trailing metadata; SDK exposes the token via callback/event and stores the latest token in client side.
- SDK helpers: provide a single helper function resume_from(token) in each language that handles attaching the token in initial request and coordinating local offsets.
- Idempotency interplay: for streaming append-type operations (client -> server append), require explicit idempotency keys for each append message or sequence ranges; for server->client streams, resume tokens + in-order sequence numbers are sufficient to resume without duplicate delivery in most cases.

Per-language ergonomic defaults (proposal):
- Python (sync/async): conservative profile default; high-level retry decorator @redwood.retry(profile='conservative') with optional idempotency_key param. Auto-gen only for convenience helpers documented as safe. Timeout defaults: 30s unary, streaming idle 60s.
- TypeScript: include RetryPolicy interface in SDK options. Default conservative profile used by client constructors. Provide middleware to attach Idempotency-Key header if provided or auto-generate when helper invoked.
- Go: context-aware retries; default conservative behavior wired into client.NewClient(opts). For streaming, supply ResumeToken type and Client.ResumeFrom(ctx, token). Encourage explicit context.WithValue for idempotency keys rather than global auto-generation.

Migration and rollout plan:
1) Documentation and RFC (this ticket) review by SDK leads + Platform (1 week).
2) Implement conservative profile in all SDKs behind feature flag (2 sprints).
3) Create migration guide and code snippets; announce opt-in period where customers can enable throughput-friendly profile.
4) After opt-in adoption > X major customers and perf validation, consider promoting throughput-friendly as an alternative documented profile (not default).

Open questions / trade-offs:
- Auto-generating keys improves DX for simple flows but may hide single-request semantics; prefer opt-in for non-trivial operations.
- TTLs for idempotency ledger are primarily server-side — we need platform agreements on default 24h and a path to extend per-customer.
- Streaming resume token extensibility: opaque tokens minimize coupling but complicate debugging — we use base64url JSON with a small, stable surface (stream_id, last_sequence) to balance visibility.
